knowledge_point.title: Solving a Challenging System of Linear Equations Using Substitution

question.:question/problem:
Using the method of substitution, find the solution of
$\{-3p + q = -9; 5p + 4q = 32$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Sometimes, it's handy to assign a number to each equation in a system, so that we can refer to them more easily:

$$
\{-3p + q + 9 = 0(1); 5p + 4q - 32 = 0(2)
$$

We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. Using equation $\color{blue}(1)$, we can solve for $q$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} q - 3p + 9 &= 0 \\ q - 3p &= -9 \\ q &= -9 + 3p \end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $q=-9+3p$ into equation $\color{red}(2)$ and solve for $p$:

$$
\begin{aligned} 4q + 5p - 32 &= 0 \\ 4(-9 + 3p) + 5p - 32 &= 0 \\ -36 + 12p + 5p - 32 &= 0 \\ -68 + 17p &= 0 \\ 17p &= 68 \\ p &= 4 \end{aligned}
$$

If we now substitute

$$
p=4
$$

into equation $\color{red}(2)$, then we can find the value of $q$:

$$
\begin{aligned} 4q + 5p - 32 &= 0 \\ 4q + 5\left(4\right) - 32 &= 0 \\ 4q + 20 - 32 &= 0 \\ 4q - 12 &= 0 \\ 4q &= 12 \\ q &= 3 \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $q=3$ and

$$
p=4
$$

, which can be written as

$$
\left(4,3\right)
$$

question.:question/problem:
Given the system of equations below, what is the value of $p - q$?

$\{5q + 55 = 0; 2p + 3q + 3 = 0$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. Using equation $\color{red}(1)$, we can solve for $q$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} 5q + 55 &= 0 \\ 5q &= -55 \\ q &= -11 \end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $q=-11$ into equation $\color{blue}(2)$ and solve for $p$:

$$
\begin{aligned} 2p + 3q + 3 &= 0 \\ 2p + 3\left(-11\right) + 3 &= 0 \\ 2p - 33 + 3 &= 0 \\ 2p &= 30 \\ p &= 15 \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $p - q = 15 - \left(-11\right) = 26$.

question.:question/problem:
Given the system of equations below, what is the value of $p - q$?

$\{5q + 60 = 0; 2p + 3q + 1 = 0$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. Using equation $\color{red}(1)$, we can solve for $q$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} 5q + 60 &= 0 \\ 5q &= -60 \\ q &= -12 \end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $q=-12$ into equation $\color{blue}(2)$ and solve for $p$:

$$
\begin{aligned} 2p + 3q + 1 &= 0 \\ 2p + 3\left(-12\right) + 1 &= 0 \\ 2p - 36 + 1 &= 0 \\ 2p &= 35 \\ p &= \dfrac{35}{2} \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $p - q = \dfrac{35}{2} - \left(-12\right) = \dfrac{59}{2}$.

question.:question/problem:
Using the method of substitution, find the solution of

$\{-7a + 2b = 18; -6a + 6b = 0$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Sometimes, it's handy to assign a number to each equation in a system, so that we can refer to them more easily:

$$
\{-7a + 2b - 18 = 0(1); -6a + 6b = 0(2)
$$

We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. Using equation $\color{blue}(2)$, we can solve for $b$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} 6b - 6a &= 0 \\ 6b - 6a &= 0 \\ 6b &= 6a \\ b &= \dfrac{6a}{6} \\ b &= a \end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $b=a$ into equation $\color{red}(1)$ and solve for $a$:

$$
\begin{aligned} 2b - 7a - 18 &= 0 \\ 2(a) - 7a - 18 &= 0 \\ 2a - 7a - 18 &= 0 \\ -18 - 5a &= 0 \\ -5a &= 18 \\ a &= -\dfrac{18}{5} \end{aligned}
$$

If we now substitute

$$
a=-\dfrac{18}{5}
$$

into equation $\color{red}(1)$, then we can find the value of $b$:

$$
\begin{aligned} 2b - 7a - 18 &= 0 \\ 2b - 7\left(-\dfrac{18}{5}\right) - 18 &= 0 \\ 2b + \dfrac{126}{5} - 18 &= 0 \\ 2b + \dfrac{36}{5} &= 0 \\ 2b &= -\dfrac{36}{5} \\ b &= -\dfrac{18}{5} \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $b=-\dfrac{18}{5}$ and

$$
a=-\dfrac{18}{5}
$$

, which can be written as

$$
\left(-\dfrac{18}{5},-\dfrac{18}{5}\right)
$$

question.:question/problem:
Solve the following system of equations:

$\{2u + 9v - 6 = 0; 2u + 6v - 8 = 0$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Sometimes, it's handy to assign a number to each equation in a system, so that we can refer to them more easily:

$$
\{2u + 9v - 6 = 0(1); 2u + 6v - 8 = 0(2)
$$

We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. Using equation $\color{blue}(2)$, we can solve for $u$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} 2u + 6v - 8 &= 0 \\ 2u + 6v &= 8 \\ 2u &= 8 - 6v \\ u &= \dfrac{8 - 6v}{2} \\ u &= 4 - 3v \end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $u=4-3v$ into equation $\color{red}(1)$ and solve for $v$:

$$
\begin{aligned} 2u + 9v - 6 &= 0 \\ 2(4 - 3v) + 9v - 6 &= 0 \\ 8 - 6v + 9v - 6 &= 0 \\ 2 + 3v &= 0 \\ 3v &= -2 \\ v &= -\dfrac{2}{3} \end{aligned}
$$

If we now substitute

$$
v=-\dfrac{2}{3}
$$

into equation $\color{red}(1)$, then we can find the value of $u$:

$$
\begin{aligned} 2u + 9v - 6 &= 0 \\ 2u + 9\left(-\dfrac{2}{3}\right) - 6 &= 0 \\ 2u - 6 - 6 &= 0 \\ 2u - 12 &= 0 \\ 2u &= 12 \\ u &= 6 \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $u=6$ and

$$
v=-\dfrac{2}{3}
$$

, which can be written as

$$
\left(6,-\dfrac{2}{3}\right)
$$

question.:question/problem:
Solve the following system of equations:

$\{4a + 3b - 54 = 0; 2a - 2b - 6 = 0$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Sometimes, it's handy to assign a number to each equation in a system, so that we can refer to them more easily:

$$
\{4a + 3b - 54 = 0(1); 2a - 2b - 6 = 0(2)
$$

We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. Using equation $\color{blue}(2)$, we can solve for $a$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} 2a - 2b - 6 &= 0 \\ 2a - 2b &= 6 \\ 2a &= 6 + 2b \\ a &= \dfrac{6 + 2b}{2} \\ a &= 3 + b \end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $a=3+b$ into equation $\color{red}(1)$ and solve for $b$:

$$
\begin{aligned} 4a + 3b - 54 &= 0 \\ 4(3 + b) + 3b - 54 &= 0 \\ 12 + 4b + 3b - 54 &= 0 \\ -42 + 7b &= 0 \\ 7b &= 42 \\ b &= 6 \end{aligned}
$$

If we now substitute

$$
b=6
$$

into equation $\color{red}(1)$, then we can find the value of $a$:

$$
\begin{aligned} 4a + 3b - 54 &= 0 \\ 4a + 3\left(6\right) - 54 &= 0 \\ 4a + 18 - 54 &= 0 \\ 4a - 36 &= 0 \\ 4a &= 36 \\ a &= 9 \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $a=9$ and

$$
b=6
$$

, which can be written as

$$
\left(9,6\right)
$$

question.:question/problem:
Using the method of substitution, find the solution of
$\{5a + b = 14; -4a - 5b = -7$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Sometimes, it's handy to assign a number to each equation in a system, so that we can refer to them more easily:

$$
\{5a + b - 14 = 0(1); -4a - 5b + 7 = 0(2)
$$

We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. Using equation $\color{blue}(1)$, we can solve for $b$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} b + 5a - 14 &= 0 \\ b + 5a &= 14 \\ b &= 14 - 5a \end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $b=14-5a$ into equation $\color{red}(2)$ and solve for $a$:

$$
\begin{aligned} -5b - 4a + 7 &= 0 \\ -5(14 - 5a) - 4a + 7 &= 0 \\ -70 + 25a - 4a + 7 &= 0 \\ -63 + 21a &= 0 \\ 21a &= 63 \\ a &= 3 \end{aligned}
$$

If we now substitute

$$
a=3
$$

into equation $\color{red}(2)$, then we can find the value of $b$:

$$
\begin{aligned} -5b - 4a + 7 &= 0 \\ -5b - 4\left(3\right) + 7 &= 0 \\ -5b - 12 + 7 &= 0 \\ -5b - 5 &= 0 \\ -5b &= 5 \\ b &= -1 \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $b=-1$ and

$$
a=3
$$

, which can be written as

$$
\left(3,-1\right)
$$

question.:question/problem:
Solve the following system of equations:

$\{-3p - 5q - 7 = 0; 3p - 3q - 9 = 0$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Sometimes, it's handy to assign a number to each equation in a system, so that we can refer to them more easily:

$$
\{-3p - 5q - 7 = 0(1); 3p - 3q - 9 = 0(2)
$$

We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. Using equation $\color{blue}(2)$, we can solve for $p$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} 3p - 3q - 9 &= 0 \\ 3p - 3q &= 9 \\ 3p &= 9 + 3q \\ p &= \dfrac{9 + 3q}{3} \\ p &= 3 + q \end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $p=3+q$ into equation $\color{red}(1)$ and solve for $q$:

$$
\begin{aligned} -3p - 5q - 7 &= 0 \\ -3(3 + q) - 5q - 7 &= 0 \\ -9 - 3q - 5q - 7 &= 0 \\ -16 - 8q &= 0 \\ -8q &= 16 \\ q &= -2 \end{aligned}
$$

If we now substitute

$$
q=-2
$$

into equation $\color{red}(1)$, then we can find the value of $p$:

$$
\begin{aligned} -3p - 5q - 7 &= 0 \\ -3p - 5\left(-2\right) - 7 &= 0 \\ -3p + 10 - 7 &= 0 \\ -3p + 3 &= 0 \\ -3p &= -3 \\ p &= 1 \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $p=1$ and

$$
q=-2
$$

, which can be written as

$$
\left(1,-2\right)
$$

question.:question/problem:
Using the method of substitution, find the solution of

$\{8x + 9y = -22; 6x + 3y = 6$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Sometimes, it's handy to assign a number to each equation in a system, so that we can refer to them more easily:

$$
\{8x + 9y + 22 = 0(1); 6x + 3y - 6 = 0(2)
$$

We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. Using equation $\color{blue}(2)$, we can solve for $y$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} 3y + 6x - 6 &= 0 \\ 3y + 6x &= 6 \\ 3y &= 6 - 6x \\ y &= \dfrac{6 - 6x}{3} \\ y &= 2 - 2x \end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $y=2-2x$ into equation $\color{red}(1)$ and solve for $x$:

$$
\begin{aligned} 9y + 8x + 22 &= 0 \\ 9(2 - 2x) + 8x + 22 &= 0 \\ 18 - 18x + 8x + 22 &= 0 \\ 40 - 10x &= 0 \\ -10x &= -40 \\ x &= 4 \end{aligned}
$$

If we now substitute

$$
x=4
$$

into equation $\color{red}(1)$, then we can find the value of $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned} 9y + 8x + 22 &= 0 \\ 9y + 8\left(4\right) + 22 &= 0 \\ 9y + 32 + 22 &= 0 \\ 9y + 54 &= 0 \\ 9y &= -54 \\ y &= -6 \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $y=-6$ and

$$
x=4
$$

, which can be written as

$$
\left(4,-6\right)
$$

question.:question/problem:
Solve the following system of equations:

$\{-6a + 2b + 23 = 0; 3a + 3b - 9 = 0$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Sometimes, it's handy to assign a number to each equation in a system, so that we can refer to them more easily:

$$
\{-6a + 2b + 23 = 0(1); 3a + 3b - 9 = 0(2)
$$

We will isolate a variable in one of the equations and then substitute it into the other equation. Using equation $\color{blue}(2)$, we can solve for $a$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} 3a + 3b - 9 &= 0 \\ 3a + 3b &= 9 \\ 3a &= 9 - 3b \\ a &= \dfrac{9 - 3b}{3} \\ a &= 3 - b \end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $a=3-b$ into equation $\color{red}(1)$ and solve for $b$:

$$
\begin{aligned} -6a + 2b + 23 &= 0 \\ -6(3 - b) + 2b + 23 &= 0 \\ -18 + 6b + 2b + 23 &= 0 \\ 5 + 8b &= 0 \\ 8b &= -5 \\ b &= -\dfrac{5}{8} \end{aligned}
$$

If we now substitute

$$
b=-\dfrac{5}{8}
$$

into equation $\color{red}(1)$, then we can find the value of $a$:

$$
\begin{aligned} -6a + 2b + 23 &= 0 \\ -6a + 2\left(-\dfrac{5}{8}\right) + 23 &= 0 \\ -6a - \dfrac{5}{4} + 23 &= 0 \\ -6a + \dfrac{87}{4} &= 0 \\ -6a &= -\dfrac{87}{4} \\ a &= \dfrac{29}{8} \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $a=\dfrac{29}{8}$ and

$$
b=-\dfrac{5}{8}
$$

, which can be written as

$$
\left(\dfrac{29}{8},-\dfrac{5}{8}\right)
$$

question.:question/problem:
Using the method of substitution, find the solution of

$\{7x + 8y = 8; 6x + 3y = 6$

$$
\{7x + 8y - 8 = 0(1); 6x + 3y - 6 = 0(2)
$$

$$
\begin{aligned} 3y + 6x - 6 &= 0 \\ 3y + 6x &= 6 \\ 3y &= 6 - 6x \\ y &= \dfrac{6 - 6x}{3} \\ y &= 2 - 2x \end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $y=2-2x$ into equation $\color{red}(1)$ and solve for $x$:

$$
\begin{aligned} 8y + 7x - 8 &= 0 \\ 8(2 - 2x) + 7x - 8 &= 0 \\ 16 - 16x + 7x - 8 &= 0 \\ 8 - 9x &= 0 \\ -9x &= -8 \\ x &= \dfrac{8}{9} \end{aligned}
$$

If we now substitute

$$
x=\dfrac{8}{9}
$$

into equation $\color{red}(1)$, then we can find the value of $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned} 8y + 7x - 8 &= 0 \\ 8y + 7\left(\dfrac{8}{9}\right) - 8 &= 0 \\ 8y + \dfrac{56}{9} - 8 &= 0 \\ 8y - \dfrac{16}{9} &= 0 \\ 8y &= \dfrac{16}{9} \\ y &= \dfrac{2}{9} \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $y=\dfrac{2}{9}$ and

$$
x=\dfrac{8}{9}
$$

, which can be written as

$$
\left(\dfrac{8}{9},\dfrac{2}{9}\right)
$$
